# Golden expected-edges fixture: tests/fixtures/golden/rust
#
# Format, xfail marker, resolution-kind column and scope: see
# tests/fixtures/golden/python/expected_edges.txt and tests/common/golden.rs.
# Only CALLS edges are scored.
#
# Baseline measured 2026-09-23: precision 1.0 (7/7), recall 1.0 (7/7),
# 5 known-failing lines. After #74 (language resolution profiles):
# precision 1.0 (30/30), recall 1.0 (30/30), 2 known-failing.
#
# The shadowing cases pin UNRESOLVED even where real Rust binds to
# `b::helper` (f2, shadow_block_use, shadow_closure_use) or `a::helper`
# (uses_helper_as_value): the shadow rule deliberately over-suppresses, and
# the pin makes any bind to the wrong `a::helper` fail loudly.

# Plain call to a private same-module fn. other_module::local_util is a
# same-named decoy.
crate::caller::entry CALLS crate::caller::local_util exact

# `use crate::helper::format_greeting` then a bare call: bound only by the
# use path, so this is specifically an import-tier match.
crate::caller::call_imported_helper CALLS crate::helper::format_greeting import

# Fully qualified `crate::` path.
crate::caller::call_crate_path CALLS crate::helper::format_greeting exact

# `super::` path (the crate root here), rewritten relative to the calling
# module before resolution — lands on the real qualname, so this is an
# exact match.
crate::caller::call_super_path CALLS crate::helper::format_greeting exact

# `self::` path, rewritten relative to the calling module (`caller`) before
# resolution — lands on the real qualname, so this is an exact match.
crate::caller::call_self_path CALLS crate::caller::local_util exact

# Method call on self. LoudGreeter::format is a same-named decoy.
crate::greeter::Greeter::greet CALLS crate::greeter::Greeter::format exact

# Receiver-typed call: `g: &Greeter`. LoudGreeter::greet is a decoy.
crate::caller::call_receiver_typed CALLS crate::greeter::Greeter::greet  # xfail: Rust params carry no receiver type for method calls

# Trait default method: Dog implements Speak without overriding speak.
# Cat::speak is a same-named decoy.
crate::caller::call_inherited CALLS crate::animals::Speak::speak  # xfail: no receiver type, and impl Trait for Type is not walked for default methods

# Ambiguous name: run exists in ambiguous_a and ambiguous_b; the use
# statement picks ambiguous_a, so this is an import-tier match (a bare-name
# fallback here would be ambiguous between the two decoys and refuse).
crate::caller::call_ambiguous CALLS crate::ambiguous_a::run import

# External path: std is never indexed.
crate::caller::call_external CALLS UNRESOLVED

# pub item calling a private item in its own module. other_module::decorate
# is a same-named private decoy.
crate::helper::format_greeting CALLS crate::helper::decorate exact

# Cross-module incoming call, through a use-import — an import-tier match.
crate::downstream::use_entry CALLS crate::caller::entry import

# `use super::helper` written inside a *nested* module (`inner`), not at
# file scope. The `super::` rewrite must use `inner`'s own enclosing module
# (this file's root), not the impl-relative or file-root special cases.
crate::nested_use::inner::calls_helper CALLS crate::nested_use::helper import

# `pub(crate) use crate::visibility_use::inner::shout` — a `pub(...)`-
# visibility `use`, not just plain `use`/`pub use`, must still parse as an
# import binding.
crate::visibility_use::calls_shout CALLS crate::visibility_use::inner::shout import

# `use prelude::announce` where `prelude` only re-exports
# `real::announce` via its own `pub use` — no symbol's qualname is exactly
# `prelude::announce`, so the import tier misses. Rust's import-miss policy
# falls through to the name tiers (unlike Refuse's default), landing here
# via bare_name.
crate::reexport_use::calls_announce CALLS crate::reexport_use::real::announce bare_name

# `use glob_source::*` at file scope binds no specific name (a glob binds
# no single resolvable name), so `run`'s bare call to `build` must stay
# unresolved — not fall through to `fixture_source::build` by way of the
# unrelated `tests` module's own (differently scoped) `use`.
crate::scoped_glob::run CALLS UNRESOLVED

# `tests`' own `use crate::scoped_glob::fixture_source::build`, scoped to
# `tests` only — an import-tier match, isolated from `run`'s glob above.
crate::scoped_glob::tests::uses_fixture_build CALLS crate::scoped_glob::fixture_source::build import

# File-scope `use crate::shadowing::a::helper`, unshadowed — an
# import-tier match.
crate::shadowing::f1 CALLS crate::shadowing::a::helper import

# `use crate::shadowing::b::helper` written inside `f2`'s own body: its
# path text mentions `helper` in a non-callee position, so the shadow rule
# suppresses the import candidate outright (round 3: no longer re-pinned to
# `b::helper` — see the round-3 header note above).
crate::shadowing::f2 CALLS UNRESOLVED

# A local `let helper = || "local";` shadows the file-scope `use` entirely:
# no import-tier candidate, and `a`/`b`'s two `helper`s make the bare-name
# fallback ambiguous too, so this stays unresolved.
crate::shadowing::f3 CALLS UNRESOLVED

# Control: no occurrence of `helper` besides the call itself, so the
# file-scope `use` still applies normally.
crate::shadowing::ok CALLS crate::shadowing::a::helper import

# Struct-shorthand destructuring (`let H { helper } = x;`) binds `helper`
# through a `shorthand_field_identifier`, a different node kind than a
# `let`/closure/`for` pattern's plain `identifier` — the shadow rule
# catches it anyway (any non-callee occurrence disqualifies), so this stays
# unresolved rather than wrongly binding to `a::helper`.
crate::shadowing::shadow_struct_shorthand CALLS UNRESOLVED

# An untyped closure parameter (`|helper| ...`) is a bare `identifier`
# directly inside `closure_parameters`, not wrapped in a `parameter` node —
# still caught, stays unresolved.
crate::shadowing::shadow_closure_param CALLS UNRESOLVED

# `match` pattern binding — stays unresolved.
crate::shadowing::shadow_match_pattern CALLS UNRESOLVED

# `if let` pattern binding — stays unresolved.
crate::shadowing::shadow_if_let CALLS UNRESOLVED

# `while let` pattern binding — stays unresolved.
crate::shadowing::shadow_while_let CALLS UNRESOLVED

# `for` loop pattern binding — stays unresolved.
crate::shadowing::shadow_for_loop CALLS UNRESOLVED

# A `use` nested in a plain block (not the function's top level) — same
# suppression as `f2` above, one level deeper.
crate::shadowing::shadow_block_use CALLS UNRESOLVED

# A `use` nested inside a closure body — same suppression as `f2`/
# `shadow_block_use` above.
crate::shadowing::shadow_closure_use CALLS UNRESOLVED

# A plain value reference (`let _ = helper;`, not a call or any pattern) is
# a non-callee occurrence too, so the later call is suppressed as well —
# documents the accepted over-suppression trade-off.
crate::shadowing::uses_helper_as_value CALLS UNRESOLVED

# `use log::info` names an external crate, not this file's own
# `util::log` submodule. The import tier must miss outright rather than
# suffix-match `util::log::info`; the name-based tiers it falls through to
# are also ambiguous (`util::log::info` vs `other::info`), so this stays
# unresolved.
crate::suffix_matching::run CALLS UNRESOLVED

# A glob `use` inside the function takes precedence over the file-scope
# `use` (rustc binds this to `b::helper`); the shadow rule suppresses it.
crate::shadowing::shadow_glob_use CALLS UNRESOLVED
